reconcile.note: Gill harmonizes the order by proposing the merchants driven out on the entry day simply returned overnight and were expelled again the next morning.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg catalogs the reversed sequence directly, noting Matthew places the cursing after the temple was purged and Mark places it before.

quotes.text: Matthew: After he purged the temple ( xxi, 12–19 ). Mark: Before he purged the temple ( xi, 12–15 ).
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), §241, on Matthew 21:19 and Mark 11:14.

sides.snippet: Let there be no fruit from you forever!
sides.verseText: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it, and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, \"Let there be no fruit from you forever!\" Immediately the fig tree withered away.

sides.snippet: May no one ever eat fruit from you again!
sides.verseText: Jesus told it, \"May no one ever eat fruit from you again!\" and his disciples heard it.
